text:
sophie: Quick heads-up — after the Docusaurus migration linkcheck is surfacing broken intra-doc fragments. Seems related to em-dashes and curly apostrophes getting normalized differently between toolchains.
omar: can you paste the CI failure lines?
sophie: from the linkcheck run:
```
[linkcheck] WARNING: ./guides/scale.mdx: anchor not found: autoscaling--best-practices
[linkcheck] WARNING: ./examples/sdk.mdx: anchor not found: initializing-the-client’s-config
```
kelly: that second one contains U+2019 (right single quote). mkdocs kept or removed it differently than docusaurus. em-dash (U+2014) shows up as `--` sometimes in our anchor map.
sophie: proposal: add a small preprocessor that normalizes only heading lines. keep it conservative — map curly quotes to straight, map ellipsis to `...`, remove zero-widths/soft-hyphen, replace em-dash with ` - `, and collapse extra spaces. I sketched a tiny Python script for readability rather than a dense sed one-liner.
```python
# docs/scripts/normalize_headings.py
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

p = Path(sys.argv[1])
text = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
lines = []
for line in text.splitlines(True):
    if line.lstrip().startswith('#'):
        # conservative replacements for heading lines only
        line = line.replace('\u2026', '...')
        line = line.replace('\u2018', "'").replace('\u2019', "'")
        line = line.replace('\u201C', '"').replace('\u201D', '"')
        line = line.replace('\u2014', ' - ')
        # remove zero-width and soft-hyphen codepoints
        line = re.sub('[\u200B-\u200D\uFEFF\u00AD]', '', line)
        line = re.sub('\s{2,}', ' ', line)
    lines.append(line)
p.write_text(''.join(lines), encoding='utf-8')
```
omar: nice — clearer than juggling sed backslashes. Add a dry-run flag so infra can preview changes.
kelly: I'll add a unit test in docs-lint that slugifies an array of sample headings with both slugify implementations and asserts equality. That should catch regressions early.
ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1589 — adds python normalizer (heading-only), unit test, and a short note in docs/migration.md explaining the normalization policy.
sophie: please tag `docs:quick` and request an expedited review. after merge we need a non-destructive backfill. infra prefers a single signed maintenance commit for the changes.
infra-bot: we'll run a dry-run backfill first and post a summary. prefer single commit for small char fixes.
omar: also suggest adding a guard so the script only updates files when a real diff exists and preserves original file mode / line endings.
kelly: patched the script to only write on diff and added a `--dry-run` flag; pushed to the PR.
ci-bot: CI queued for PR #1589 (linkcheck + docs-lint + tests)
ci-bot: CI passed for PR #1589
infra-bot: dry-run backfill shows 29 files would be modified. scheduling maintenance run in 30m to apply changes as a single commit by infra-bot.
infra-bot: backfill applied: 29 files modified, commit "docs: normalize heading punctuation to prevent fragment mismatches" pushed by infra-bot
sophie: reran linkcheck on the preview build — fragment warnings disappeared. thanks team.
kelly: added a one-paragraph note in docs/migration.md listing the characters normalized and the rationale (stability of slugs across toolchains).
omar: closing thread. :white_check_mark:
